overall_summary: Deduplicated performance analysis reveals that 'What If' space scenarios and extreme planetary physics (particularly weird planetary environments and liquid/diamond/ice extremes) are heavily outperforming standard static facts and general psychology. Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' show exceptionally high views-per-day and strong engagement rates (likes-per-view) compared to older or simpler biological facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos featuring 'What If You Fell Into...' formats (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y, 8KEl0_pJ_68, 6pwazIPnOHw) consistently achieve top-tier views (970-1029+ views) and high like counts relative to their age.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' extreme physics scenarios involving bizarre cosmic bodies rather than simple declarative statements.

winning_patterns.evidence: Topics centered on extreme planetary conditions—such as Venus's day/year paradox (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and ultra-dark exoplanets (v1rrcZLdp4U)—drive rapid traction and solid viewer retention hooks.
winning_patterns.action: Focus upcoming space content on lesser-known exoplanet anomalies and extreme astrophysical phenomena.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) and general memory/song loops stagnate below 15-50 views even weeks after publishing.

weak_patterns.action: Reframe static facts into active, immersive 'What If' questions or mind-bending existential paradoxes.
